mathematical_scope: The support theorem is valid for the stated model: if F=M_t B_t^-1 ... B_1^-1 M_0 and each B_i has at most s nonzeros per row while M_i are monomial, then F^-1 has row support at most s^t. A dense inverse Fourier matrix requires s^t>=N. The integer loop computes ceil(log_s N) without floating logarithms. The random routine tracks Boolean possible support, so numerical cancellations cannot invalidate its upper bound.
input_and_guard_coverage: support_lower_bound asserts s>=2,N>=2, but not integrality. random_row_sparsity_audit has no explicit domain checks for N,s,t. For positive N and s>N, its while len(choices)<s can never finish: choices are contained in range(N). N=0 reaches max(empty), negative t silently performs no stages, noninteger s has unclear rounded behavior.
cost_and_scaling: Lower-bound loop uses O(log_s N) multiplications. Random support storage can grow to N² elements; naive set unions per factor can take O(N·s·min(N,s^level)) work. Sampling s distinct values becomes expensive as s approaches N. It is a dense structural audit, not an O(N) Green application.
test_evidence: Three support-bound values and four finite random cases appear in phase15 final test class. None covers s>N, N=0, or negative t, and that entire class is omitted in direct script invocation. No tests run here.
dependency_identity: Standard-library random; math imported unused. No unreviewed local dependency.

findings.finding: Deterministic nontermination for s>N: at most N distinct indices can ever enter choices, so the while loop cannot terminate. This is a source proof, not an executed failure.
The source correctly excludes sums of Green solves and stages with nonsparse inverses. Applying this support veto to those models would exceed its mathematical scope.

acceptance_boundary: Accept the sparse-inverse product support argument and small valid-domain Boolean controls. Repair input guards before treating the random helper as a general callable audit.
